Log of BLAST searches

Source: R/blast_log.R
blast_log_path.Rd

When a log directory is set, each search made by parallel_blast() adds one line to BLASTr_logs/blastr_runs.tsv inside it (the folder and file are created when needed). The directory is taken, in this order, from the log_dir argument of parallel_blast(), the option BLASTr.log_dir and the environment variable BLASTR_LOG_DIR; with none of them, nothing is logged. In background jobs, the line is written when the results are collected with blast_job_result().

Each line has:

  • the run: run_id, start, end, host, user, mode (foreground/background), function (parallel_blast() or parallel_blast_hsps()), blastr_version, blast_version, job_dir;

  • the sequences: n_input (as given), n_seqs (unique ones searched), n_invalid and their length distribution (len_min, len_q25, len_median, len_mean, len_q75, len_max);

  • the database(s): db_path, n_dbs, db_gb (sum), db_volumes, ram_gb, fits_ram;

  • the strategy and settings: total_cores, processes, threads, mt_mode, batch_size, n_batches, task, num_alignments, search_alignments, perc_id, perc_qcov_hsp, check_n, check_tolerance;

  • the cost: wall_s, cpu_s (CPU time of the BLAST processes), cpu_h, cpu_efficiency (cpu_s over wall_s times the threads in use), n_batches_failed, n_seqs_failed;

  • the identifications: n_with_hits, pct_with_hits, pct_best_id, pct_check_id (both over all sequences), id1_median (median identity of the first hit) and pct_id1_ge_99, pct_id1_ge_97 (sequences whose first hit has identity of at least 99% / 97%). For parallel_blast_hsps(), pct_best_id and pct_check_id are NA and the first hit is the first HSP of the best subject.

When a newer BLASTr adds columns, the file is rewritten with all of them (missing values as NA).

Usage

blast_log_path(log_dir = NULL)

read_blast_log(log_dir = NULL)

Arguments

log_dir

Directory where the BLASTr_logs folder is kept. NULL uses the option and the environment variable described above.

Value

blast_log_path() returns the path of the log file, or NULL when no log directory is set. read_blast_log() returns the log as a tibble.

See also

Other search functions: blast_job(), blast_strategy(), exit_codes(), parallel_blast(), parallel_blast_hsps()

Examples

log_dir <- tempfile("blastr_logs_")
blast_log_path(log_dir)
#> /tmp/RtmpWKof0T/blastr_logs_19b7d752683/BLASTr_logs/blastr_runs.tsv

# needs BLAST+ (see install_dependencies())
if (has_blast()) {
  fasta <- system.file("extdata", "minimal_db_blast.fasta", package = "BLASTr")
  db <- file.path(tempdir(), "minimal_db_blast")
  make_blast_db(fasta, db_path = db)
  seqs <- readLines(system.file("extdata", "seqs_test.txt", package = "BLASTr"))
  res <- parallel_blast(seqs, db, log_dir = log_dir)
  read_blast_log(log_dir)
}
